text:
Maria: quick post from today's perf run on 4xA100 (40GB). TP=2 PP=2 DP=1. KV-cache currently sharded by contiguous layer ranges (0..L/4, L/4..L/2, ...). seeing ~18% tail spikes on token latency. suspect KV sync + short kernel gaps.

Maria: timeline excerpt from profiler:
```
step 4128
  forward compute: 3.4ms
  local kv update: 0.6ms
  all-reduce(kv_sync): 1.2ms
  kernel dispatch gap: 0.9ms
  end-to-end token: 6.1ms  // tail dominated by AR + gaps
```

Aj: same pattern in my runs. AR on "hot" shards creates cross-device stalls when PP/TP split forces hops. two pragmatic levers: (1) hot-replication for a small set of top blocks to avoid frequent AR, (2) reduce AR latency with fp16 buffers and micro-compression + async ops.

Sophia: we tried a hybrid earlier: replicate last 3-6 transformer blocks across devices and shard the rest. result: tail went from ~18% -> ~12%, cost: +5-7GB/device depending on model depth. worth considering as route-level policy.

Derek: kernel scheduling also matters. today runtime schedules big matmuls then blocks on AR. if we interleave attention kernels and kv-pack chunks, AR can progress in background and reduce observed gaps.

Derek: tiny sketch of scheduling change we tested:
```
// interleave KV packing and attention to improve overlap
for layer in layers_with_remote_shards:
  launch(kv_pack_part(layer, 0))
  launch(attention_kernel(layer, small_slice))
  // allow all-reduce to run async
  launch(kv_pack_part(layer, 1))
```

Aj: also saw ~20% AR time drop in microbench when switching comm buffers to fp16 + lightweight delta compression in the fast path. caveat: need correctness checks for accumulation precision.

Sophia: batching heuristics note: if device occupancy < 0.7, holding an extra 3-6ms batch window (adaptive) boosts batching without blowing SLO tail for our latency-sensitive routes. combined with hot-replica this yields best cost/latency tradeoff in our sims.

Maria: proposal: run a 4xA100 experiment matrix and compare:
- BASELINE: contiguous-layer shard (current)
- HYBRID-REPL: replicate top N layers (hot-replica) + shard rest
- PLACEMENT-GREEDY: per-layer placement minimizing AR hops across TP groups
- SCHED-INTERLEAVE: Derek's interleave + async/fused AR ops
- ADAPTIVE-BATCH: Sophia's adaptive hold window

Maria: owners: baseline infra, hybrid = Sophia, placement = Aj, interleave = Derek, adaptive batch = Maria. can perf CI run these with both synthetic and representative prompt sets?

perf-bot: perf CI started: kv-hot-replica-experiments/1903456789. running 4xA100 matrix across combos. ETA ~50m. results will be posted to #eng-runtime. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Aj: one more angle: DP (request-level replication) removes AR but scales cost linearly with replica factor. maybe allow per-route replication policy: low-latency routes get replication, high-throughput routes stay sharded. dynamic request-level routing could switch modes based on current tail and cost budget.

Sophia: agree. expose route config like {policy: "hybrid", hot_layers: 4, batch_hold_ms: 4} would make tuning straightforward for customers.

Derek: for better attribution, add NVTX ranges around AR and small metrics (bytes/sec, AR latency p50/p95) to the console so we can see exact overlap and where kernel gaps happen.

Maria: action items: brief RFC summarizing matrix + perf CI links, owners start experiments. Derek to land interleave prototype in a feature branch. Sophia to run hybrid memory/cost profile. Aj to run per-layer placement sim and comm microbench. I'll follow up with a tiny RFC and schedule a 30m sync after CI results. thanks! :+1:

Maria: @perf-bot when CI finishes can you attach the raw nvprof timeline link?
